issues.issue: Em-dashes present in the prompt, which its own Do-nots forbid. At least two: "`src/w1_core/correction/rules.py` — `apply_terminology(text, mode)` iterates..." and "`src/w1_core/correction/transliterate.py` — 127 lines, complete and working" (both in "The multi-mode system that was deleted").
issues.fix: Replace both em-dashes with a colon or a period, then sweep the whole document for U+2014 before shipping. Keep the en-dash in "U+0A80–U+0AFF" (correct usage, not an em-dash).

issues.issue: Five of the seven modes (Prompt Engineer, Polish, Formal, Street, Summarisation) are model-driven text rewriting, but w1 has no text-generation capability at all and the prompt never says so. Verified: pyproject.toml runtime deps are pydantic 2.13.4 / rapidfuzz 3.14.5 / jellyfish 1.2.1 / pyyaml 6.0.3 / numpy 2.4.6, the optional extras are whisper backends only, and grep for anthropic|openai|llama|mlx_lm|ollama across src/ and scripts/ returns nothing. The prompt simultaneously demands "where it runs (on-device or otherwise)" per mode, says "Where the brief is silent, ask rather than invent", forbids quiet network calls, and imposes SOR-2 on new deps. The implementer cannot produce output requirement 2 without either guessing an inference engine or stalling.
issues.fix: Add to Context: "w1 today contains no text-generation model. The correction chain is purely deterministic (rapidfuzz + jellyfish). Every model-driven mode requires a new inference layer that does not exist." Then require the architecture delta to state the fork as a user decision: local (mlx-lm or llama.cpp with a named model, bundle-size and latency cost) vs API (network, contradicts the on-device promise at src/w1_macos/settings_window.py:168 and the pyproject description "fully on-device"). Add it to the Conflict-resolution open questions.

issues.issue: src/w1_data/diacritics.json is missed entirely, and it is the exact implementation of the user's hardest contract. It is a 12-entry stripping map (ṁ→m, ṭ→t, ṣ→sh, ś→sh, ṇ→n, ī→i, ū→u, ṛ→r, ṅ→n, ḍ→d, ħ→h, ñ→n, deliberately excluding ā), it is one of the 5 permitted w1_data datasets, and loader.py:66 loads it into RuleData.diacritics — but no correction step consumes it (engine.py is cleanup, mask, fuzzy, unmask only). It is a THIRD orphan, not two. The draft omits it from the Data list and points the ā-only chokepoint solely at transliterate.py, which handles Gujarati script to Roman, not already-Romanised diacritics to ā-only. Both paths are needed to honour "no other letter carries a diacritic".
issues.fix: Add diacritics.json (12 entries) to the Data bullet; list it as the third orphan (loaded at loader.py:66, consumed by nothing); specify the ā-only chokepoint as covering both inputs (Gujarati script via transliterate.py, Roman diacritics via the diacritics map). Note that the deleted CorrectionMode.dictation docstring on main listed "diacritics" as part of the dictation chain, which is when the wiring was lost.

issues.issue: Join meeting mode and Meeting mode's system-audio capture are posed as implementation details when they are architectural forks that collide with the stated constraints. "How Join meeting mode attaches to Teams, Google Meet and Zoom" has no local-only answer; a bot joining a call is a hosted-service pattern. Conflict rule 4 covers only "a Wispr Flow behaviour requires a server", and joining meetings is not a Wispr Flow behaviour, so nothing in the prompt reaches it. Separately, packaging/w1.entitlements grants only com.apple.security.device.audio-input; capturing incoming meeting audio also needs ScreenCaptureKit or CoreAudio process taps (macOS 14.2+) with Screen Recording consent, or a virtual device.
issues.fix: Broaden conflict rule 4 to "any required behaviour", not just Wispr Flow behaviours. Add the entitlement fact to Context and require the delta to name the system-audio mechanism plus the new entitlement/TCC prompt. For Join meeting, require an explicit fork (local automation of the desktop clients vs a hosted joiner) with the privacy consequence stated, marked as a user decision.

issues.issue: Mode triggers are demanded but undecidable. Output requirement 1 requires "trigger (hotkey or menu)" for all seven modes; the brief supplies exactly one (Opt+1 for Polish) and the existing config has only hotkey '<alt_r>' with push-to-talk/toggle. The stance rule "Where the brief is silent, ask rather than invent" then blocks filling the other six, so the implementer either invents six bindings against instruction or stalls mid-spec.
issues.fix: Resolve it in the prompt: either state a convention as an explicit proposal to confirm ("Opt+1 is fixed by the brief; propose Opt+2..Opt+N for the remaining modes and flag as pending confirmation"), or move mode triggers into the Conflict-resolution open questions and drop "trigger" from the per-mode required fields.

issues.issue: Internal contradiction between the brief's headline requirement and a Do-not. The brief says "make it serve the same function as wispr flow", but the Do-nots say "Do not invent modes, settings, or features beyond the seven modes and the surfaces named above." Any Wispr Flow function not enumerated (custom dictionary/snippets, per-app tone, mid-utterance auto-edits, latency parity, onboarding) is foreclosed by the Do-not while being mandated by the Task.
issues.fix: Separate shipping from proposing: "Do not ship modes, settings, or features beyond the seven modes and the named surfaces. Where Wispr Flow does something w1 does not and it is not on that list, record it in a separate 'parity gaps' section for the user to approve; do not build it unasked."

(a) Constraints claims scripts/ingest_glossary_pdf.py and scripts/sync_rules_from_ts.py "both hardcode paths into ~/Desktop/Repositories/Mandir/ and therefore cannot regenerate their data as written" — only ingest_glossary_pdf.py:22 hardcodes an absolute Desktop path; sync_rules_from_ts.py:32-33 derives _REPOS = _HERE.parents[2] and exposes an overridable DEFAULT_SRC, so it is relocatable and only needs the Mandir source located.
